text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — Voltix Retail showing a sharp usage drop since last Wednesday. Their Dedicated trial tokens are down ~65% week-over-week. Also heard that their new PM Tess took over procurement and is running a parallel POC with NimbusAI.
Liam O'Rourke: Ugh, timeline? Renewal in 7 weeks?
Maya Chen: Renewal notice in 7w. Current MOUs say they want predictable latency for peak loads — our Dedicated perf was a selling point.
Jonah Patel: Pushed a quick query, here's the high-level signal:```
active_users_weekly: 18 -> 6
avg_tokens_per_request: 450 -> 340
top_routes: /embed (big drop), /generate (smaller)
last_full_prod_call: 2024-10-18
```
Priya Shah: Do we know why embed usage dropped specifically? Are they switching architecture or the competitor offers cheaper embeddings?
Maya Chen: Voltix mentioned cost + latency in their last call with Liam. Tess asked for a price/latency comparison.
Liam O'Rourke: I forwarded our latency report and pricing summary yesterday. No reply yet. Tess is scheduling short demos with both vendors this week.
cs-bot: Ticket created: CS-4521 "Voltix renewal triage - usage drop & Nimbus POC" assigned to Maya, Jonah. Reminder set for 48h.
Maya Chen: Proposed triage plan: 1) Quick win outreach (2 diff touchpoints) 2) Curated pricing/latency one-pager vs Nimbus 3) Offer 2-week dedicated burst credit + technical deep-dive 4) Collect failing prompt sets / integration blockers 5) Schedule joint call with Tess + Eng.
Jonah Patel: I can assemble: - short latency table (p95/median) - cost delta assumptions for embeds (8-bit quant profile) - sample request traces. ETA: EOD today.
Priya Shah: I'll draft the one-pager and a 15-min demo script highlighting our latency SLOs, cache/batching benefits, and rollback policies. Need any customer-specific numbers?
Maya Chen: Yes — include: current committed capacity, recent peak QPS, and their 99th p99 latency on Dedicated (we drove p99 to ~120ms on last bench). Also add fallback policy notes (can route to hosted lighter model).
Liam O'Rourke: I'll ask Tess if procurement is open to a short performance SLA for the pilot — could be a differentiator. Also put me on the call if she accepts.
Jonah Patel: Quick snippet I'll attach to the one-pager:```
Benchmark summary (voltix-trial):
- embed model: p50 30ms, p95 85ms, p99 130ms
- gen model: p50 80ms, p95 220ms
- observed cache hit-rate: 18% (we can bump)
```
Maya Chen: Meeting ask: 30-min with Tess + Eng lead. Goal: unblock integration, surface cost sensitivity, and offer performance burst. Who can join tomorrow 11am PT?
Liam O'Rourke: I can.
Jonah Patel: I'm free.
Priya Shah: I can do 11am PT for the quick demo.
Maya Chen: Action items: - Maya: lead outreach + run meeting - Jonah: attach metrics + traces (EOD) - Priya: one-pager + demo script (EOD) - Liam: procurement contact + competitive intel (checkback in 24h)
Maya Chen: If Tess pushes Nimbus pricing, we should be ready to offer a focused cost/latency pilot with a 2-week performance SLA and a single integration engineer slot. Thoughts?
Liam O'Rourke: Agree. Make the pilot scoped and timeboxed; don't expand feature set. Keep it focused on embedding throughput/latency.
Priya Shah: I'll include suggested success metrics for the pilot in the one-pager (target embed p95 <100ms, >60% cache hit, and <10% error rate).
Jonah Patel: Also adding a quick troubleshooting checklist: common integration mistakes (wrong batching, not reusing KV cache, large token prefixes).
Maya Chen: Cool. I'll ping Tess now with a calendar invite and the CS-4521 ticket link.
cs-bot: Reminder: CS-4521 follow-up in 48 hours (assigned: Maya, Jonah).
Maya Chen: Thanks team — will update thread after call. :thumbsup:
